description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between the minimum average displacement error (minADE₂₀, in meters) and the ratio of training data used for different models, with lower values indicating better performance. The x-axis, labeled "Ratio," spans from 0.2 to 1.0 in increments of 0.2, representing the proportion of the full training dataset used. The y-axis, labeled "minADE₂₀ (←)," ranges from 0.55 to 0.75, indicating the minimum average displacement error in meters. The plot includes five models: Head Tuning (blue, solid line with circle markers), FT (orange, solid line with circle markers), LoRA 16 (red, solid line with circle markers), LoRA 64 (purple, solid line with circle markers), and a baseline model (green, solid line with circle markers). As the ratio increases from 0.2 to 1.0, the minADE₂₀ for all models generally decreases. At a ratio of 0.2, Head Tuning starts at approximately 0.61 m, FT at 0.77 m, LoRA 16 at 0.74 m, LoRA 64 at 0.73 m, and the baseline model at 0.68 m. By a ratio of 1.0, the minADE₂₀ for Head Tuning stabilizes around 0.60 m, FT decreases to about 0.68 m, LoRA 16 decreases to approximately 0.60 m, LoRA 64 decreases to around 0.61 m, and the baseline model decreases to about 0.53 m. The baseline model consistently achieves the lowest minADE₂₀ across all ratios, while FT shows the highest error throughout the range.
